questions.q: In our cells, food is broken down with oxygen to release energy. Name this process.
questions.explain: Respiration is the process in our cells that breaks down food with oxygen to release energy. Breathing only moves air in and out of the lungs.

questions.q: Breathing brings air into our lungs. Explain why we need to breathe.
choices: to take in oxygen for respiration
questions.explain: Our cells need oxygen for respiration. Breathing takes in the oxygen and gets rid of carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Glucose reacts with oxygen in our cells. State the products of respiration.
questions.explain: In respiration glucose reacts with oxygen to give carbon dioxide, water and energy.

questions.q: Respiration takes place in our cells. State the substances needed for respiration.
questions.explain: Respiration needs glucose and oxygen. Carbon dioxide and water are its products.

questions.q: Breathed-in air passes through the nose. Name the tube it enters next.
questions.explain: Air goes from the nose into the windpipe. The gullet carries food, not air.

questions.q: Breathed-in air passes through the windpipe. Name the tubes it enters next.
questions.explain: The windpipe splits into two bronchi, one going to each lung.

questions.q: Breathed-in air passes through the bronchi. Name the part it reaches next.
questions.explain: The bronchi lead into smaller tubes that end in tiny air sacs in the lungs.

questions.q: In the lungs, oxygen leaves the air sacs. Name what it passes into.
questions.explain: Oxygen passes from the air sacs into the blood. The blood carries it to all the cells.

questions.q: Breathed-in air has just entered the bronchi. Name the tube it has just left.
questions.explain: Air passes through the windpipe before it reaches the bronchi. So it has just left the windpipe.

questions.q: Air enters the body through the nose. State one function of the nose.
choices: traps dirt and germs in air
questions.explain: The nose traps dirt and germs in the air with its hairs and mucus. It also warms and moistens the air.

questions.q: Cells in the windpipe make a sticky substance that traps dust. Name this substance.
questions.explain: Cells in the windpipe make sticky mucus. The mucus traps dust and germs before they reach the lungs.

questions.q: The windpipe splits into two tubes going to the lungs. Name these tubes.
questions.explain: The windpipe splits into two tubes called bronchi. One goes to each lung.

questions.q: The ribs form a cage around the chest. State the function of the ribcage.
questions.explain: The ribcage is a cage of bones around the chest. It protects the lungs and the heart.

questions.q: Name the muscle under the lungs that separates the chest from the belly.
questions.explain: The diaphragm is a sheet of muscle under the lungs. It separates the chest from the belly and helps us breathe.

questions.q: A person chokes while eating. Name the tube that the food has entered.
questions.explain: Choking happens when food goes down the windpipe instead of the gullet and blocks the airway.

questions.q: When we swallow, food goes down a tube to the stomach. Name this tube.
questions.explain: Swallowed food goes down the gullet to the stomach. The windpipe carries air to the lungs.

questions.q: Inhale means breathe in. Describe the movement of the ribcage when we inhale.
questions.explain: When we inhale, the rib muscles pull the ribcage upwards and outwards. This makes the chest bigger, so air rushes into the lungs.

questions.q: Inhale means breathe in. Describe the movement of the diaphragm when we inhale.
questions.explain: When we inhale, the diaphragm contracts and flattens, so it moves down. This makes the chest bigger and air flows into the lungs.

questions.q: Exhale means breathe out. Describe the movement of the ribcage when we exhale.
questions.explain: When we exhale, the ribcage moves downwards and inwards. This makes the chest smaller and pushes air out of the lungs.

questions.q: Exhale means breathe out. Describe the movement of the diaphragm when we exhale.
questions.explain: When we exhale, the diaphragm relaxes and moves up into a dome shape. This makes the chest smaller and pushes air out.

questions.q: In the chest, the diaphragm contracts and moves down. Identify the process taking place.
questions.explain: The diaphragm contracts and moves down when we breathe in. This makes the chest bigger, so air flows into the lungs.

questions.q: In the chest, the ribcage moves downwards and inwards. Identify the process taking place.
questions.explain: The ribcage moves downwards and inwards when we breathe out. This makes the chest smaller, so air is pushed out.

questions.q: Exhaled air is breathed-out air. Name the two gases it has more of.
questions.explain: Respiration makes carbon dioxide and water. So breathed-out air has more carbon dioxide and more water vapour than breathed-in air.

questions.q: Inhaled air is breathed-in air. State the percentage of oxygen in inhaled air.
questions.explain: Breathed-in air is about 21% oxygen. Most of the rest is nitrogen, at about 78%.

questions.q: Exhaled air is breathed-out air. State the percentage of oxygen in exhaled air.
questions.explain: Breathed-out air is about 16% oxygen. Some of the oxygen breathed in was taken into the blood for respiration.

questions.q: Exhaled air is breathed-out air. State the percentage of carbon dioxide in exhaled air.
questions.explain: Breathed-out air is about 4% carbon dioxide. Breathed-in air has only about 0.04%.

questions.q: A gas is 21% of breathed-in air and 16% of breathed-out air. Identify the gas.
questions.explain: Oxygen is about 21% of breathed-in air and about 16% of breathed-out air. The body uses some of it for respiration.

questions.q: A gas is 78% of both breathed-in and breathed-out air. Identify the gas.
questions.explain: Nitrogen is about 78% of the air. Our body does not use it, so the amount is the same in breathed-in and breathed-out air.

questions.q: Breathed-in air has 21% oxygen. Breathed-out air has 16% oxygen. Calculate the difference.
questions.explain: Difference = 21% - 16% = 5%.

questions.q: Exhaled air has less oxygen than inhaled air. Explain why.
choices: oxygen is stored in the bronchi
questions.explain: Some of the oxygen breathed in passes into the blood. Our cells use it in respiration, so less oxygen is left in the air we breathe out.

questions.q: Name the substance used to test for carbon dioxide.
questions.explain: Limewater is used to test for carbon dioxide. It turns chalky (milky) when carbon dioxide is bubbled through it.

questions.q: Dry cobalt chloride paper is placed in water vapour. Describe its colour change.
questions.explain: Dry cobalt chloride paper is blue. It turns pink when it touches water, so it is used to test for water.

questions.q: Breathed-in and breathed-out air are bubbled through limewater. Predict which turns it milky faster.
questions.explain: Breathed-out air has much more carbon dioxide than breathed-in air. So it turns limewater milky faster.

questions.q: Name the substance in cigarette smoke that makes smokers addicted.
questions.explain: Nicotine is the substance in cigarette smoke that makes smokers addicted.

questions.q: Name the substance in cigarette smoke that can cause lung cancer.
questions.explain: Tar is a sticky substance in cigarette smoke. It collects in the lungs and can cause lung cancer.

questions.q: Hair-like structures in the windpipe sweep out dust. Describe the effect of tar on them.
questions.explain: Tar is sticky. It makes the tiny hairs in the windpipe stick together so they cannot sweep out dust and mucus.

questions.q: Chemicals in cigarette smoke can block blood vessels. Name the disease this can cause.
questions.explain: Chemicals in cigarette smoke can narrow and block blood vessels. Blocked blood vessels to the heart cause heart disease.

questions.q: In a smoker, the bronchi become swollen and sore. Name this disease.
questions.explain: Bronchitis is when the bronchi become swollen and sore. Smoking is a common cause.

questions.q: A passive smoker does not smoke. Explain why passive smokers can still get smoking diseases.
choices: they have too many air sacs
they breathe in too much oxygen
they make tar in their lungs
questions.explain: Passive smokers breathe in other people's cigarette smoke. So the harmful substances in the smoke still reach their lungs.
